To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

T cells from children with type 1 and longstanding type 1 diabetes have an impaired expression of the interleulin‐12 receptor β‐chain, which is associated with a reduced type 1 and increased type 2 polarization.

children with newly diagnosed and with longstanding type 1 diabetes have aberrant type 1 cytokines‐induced expression levels of the interleukine‐12 receptor β‐2 chain on peripheral blood CD4 and CD 8 T cells.
children with T1D had decreased expression of the IL12Rβ2 on CD4 and 8 cells and increased secretion of the Th2 cytokine IL‐13.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel aspect of T‐cell polarization in T1D.
the aberrant regulation of the IL‐R12β2 chain on type‐1‐cytokine‐stimulated peripheral T cells, which may play a role in the pathogenesis of T1D.
the aberrant regulation of the IL‐R12β2 chain on peripheral blood T cells of T1D patients, which may be a consequence of a disturbed T‐cell polarization towards the Th1 phenotype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL‐12R β2 chain expression is decreased in T1D patients and that this decrease may be related to the impaired type 1 T‐cell polarization in patients with T1D.
T cells from children with T1D show aberrant polarization towards type 2 cells and poor polarization towards type I cells.
T cells from patients have an aberrant regulation of the IL‐2 receptor β2 chain and that this aberrant regulation may be involved in the development of T1D.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T1D is associated with an aberrant expression of the IL12Rβ2 on peripheral blood T cells, which may be involved in the development and maintenance of T1D.
the aberrant regulation of the IL‐R12β2 chain on peripheral blood T cells in T1D may contribute to the impaired T‐cell polarization in these patients.
T1D‐related immune dysregulation is characterized by aberrant regulation of IL‐12 receptor β 2 chain on type1 cytokine‐activated T lymphocytes, which may play a role in the development of T1D.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the aberrant polarization of peripheral blood lymphocytes from patients with T1D is associated with a decreased expression of IL‐12 receptors, which may contribute to the pathogenesis of this disease.
aberrant expression of IL‐12 receptors on T cells from patients may be involved in this aberrant polarization.
the IL‐12 receptor β‐chain is aberrantly expressed on T cells from patients affected by T1D and that this is associated with a decreased polarization of T cells towards type 1.
